Archives can be encrypted, copied to a remote destination, pruned by a retention policy and restored in place or as a new tenant — from the Desk, the TUI or the CLI. ``` backups//____.tar.gz[.enc] backups//.json ← manifest + size + SHA-256 ``` | Archive content | | |-----------------|--| | `manifest.json` | Format and version, tenant, kind, date | | `database/` | The database dump | | `site/` | `sites//` without its database and sessions — `config.json` (whose key decrypts the tenant's stored secrets), uploads, themes | | Kind | Made | |------|------| | `manual` | From the Desk, TUI or CLI | | `scheduled` | By the schedule in Backup Settings | | `pre-update` | Automatically, before an app is installed or updated | | `pre-restore` | Automatically, before a restore overwrites the site | | `uploaded` | An archive uploaded from elsewhere, to restore it here | "}},{"node":"backups-settings","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Backup Settings","key":"backups-settings","id":"backups-settings","name":"backups-settings","value":"## Backup Settings Open **Backup Settings** in the Desk (one per tenant). ### Schedule | Field | Description | |-------|-------------| | **Back up automatically** | Turn scheduled backups on | | **Frequency** | Every day or every week (+ **On**: the weekday) | | **At** | Server time, `HH:MM` | | **Include files** | Include uploads in the archive | The core's scheduler checks every hour and runs the backup once the time has passed. ### Retention Scheduled backups follow **grandfather–father–son**: keep the newest backup of each of the last *N* days, *N* ISO weeks and *N* months. | Field | Default | |-------|---------| | **Keep daily backups** | 7 | | **Keep weekly backups** | 4 | | **Keep monthly backups** | 3 | Manual backups and safety snapshots (pre-update, pre-restore) keep their own most recent ones. ### Encryption Turn on **Encrypt backups** and set a **Passphrase**: the whole archive is encrypted with AES-256-GCM, its key derived from your passphrase (scrypt). It is your passphrase — not the tenant's key — because the tenant's `config.json` travels inside the archive. **Without the passphrase an encrypted backup can't be restored.** ### Remote copy **Copy backups to** a second place, so a lost server doesn't take its backups with it: | Destination | Settings | |-------------|----------| | **This server only** | — | | **S3-compatible** | Endpoint, region, bucket, access key, secret key, folder — AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, DigitalOcean Spaces, MinIO, Google Cloud Storage | | **SFTP** | Host, port, username, password or private key file, remote folder | | **WebDAV** | Folder URL, username, password (Nextcloud, ownCloud…) | | **Google Drive** | OAuth client ID and secret, then **Connect** an account; folder ID | Secrets are stored encrypted. The last run's time, status, file and message are shown at the bottom (*Partial* means the local backup worked but the remote copy didn't). "}},{"node":"backups-restore","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Backups Page & Restore","key":"backups-restore","id":"backups-restore","name":"backups-restore","value":"## The Backups Page **Backups** in the Desk lists local and remote archives of the site: | Action | Who | |--------|-----| | **Back up now** | Users with permission | | **Download** (fetched from the destination when only there) · **Inspect** (manifest) | Users with permission | | **Upload** an archive made elsewhere | Users with permission | | **Restore** · **Delete** · connect a destination | **Administrator** only | ### Restoring A restore over the current site runs in the background: a **pre-restore** snapshot is taken first, then the site answers "restoring" until it re-opens on the restored data. You confirm by typing the site's name. To restore into a **new** tenant instead (to inspect old data, or move a site to another server), use the CLI with `--as`. "}},{"node":"backups-cli","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"CLI & TUI","key":"backups-cli","id":"backups-cli","name":"backups-cli","value":"## From the Terminal The backup engine works without booting the framework, so a tenant that won't start can still be backed up and restored. ```bash yarn backup # last backup of every tenant yarn backup create [--local] # --local: keep it on this server only yarn backup list # local and remote backups yarn backup restore [--as ] [--passphrase

] [--yes] yarn backup delete [--local|--remote] ``` A restore **in place** needs the tenant turned off (`yarn tenant off `); `--as ` restores into a new tenant. In the TUI, select a tenant and press **`B`**: `n` backs up now, `r` restores the selected archive, `d` deletes it. ### Moving a site to another server 1. `yarn backup create my-site` on the old server (download it from the Desk if it isn't in a remote destination). 2. Copy the archive to `backups/my-site/` on the new server — or upload it from the new site's Backups page. 3. `yarn backup restore my-site --as my-site` (it creates the tenant on the new server). 4. Point the domain to the new server. "}}]}]
